context: Standalone python checker with no third-party deps so the Actions job is trivial; run it in CI on pull_request to main and document in README.
description: skill-sync-skills invariant (c) (docs/propagation.md) requires skill-sync.lock to be regenerated in the same commit as any skill edit, but nothing enforces it: PRs #9 and #10 merged skill edits (SHARED/commit-framework, SHARED/review-protocol) with stale lock hashes, silently breaking lock integrity on main until PR #11 repaired the instances. The class remains unguarded — the repo has no CI and no pre-commit hook. Deliverable: scripts/verify_lock.py in the canonical repo that recomputes sha256/size for every lock entry against the tree, fails on any mismatch, and fails on skills listed in skill-sync.yaml but absent from the lock (the accidental-docs-drop class, instance-fixed in PR #11); wired as a required GitHub Actions check on PRs to main. Discovered 2026-07-29 during the docs-skill restoration.

preserves.behavior: Existing lock format and skill-sync CLI compatibility; Joe's identity on commits

verifications.description: checker exists and passes on the live checkout
verifications.expected: exit 0 once the checker is written and main lock is consistent
a workflow on PRs to main invokes the checker

work_units.evidence: scripts/verify_lock.py (PR #13 on skill-sync-skills). Fails on: declared-but-unlocked skill, locked-but-undeclared skill, locked file missing from tree, sha256/size mismatch, and a file present under a locked skill that the lock never recorded - the last being the case a hash comparison alone cannot catch, since adding a file leaves every recorded hash correct. Prior art examined before writing: skill-sync CLI 'verify' checks committed mirrors in consumer projects and reports 'No tracked targets to verify' here; 'status' compares installed targets under ~/.claude/skills, not this checkout, and reported 'clean' while real drift existed; 'validate' checks manifest portability. Reuse decision: genuinely new, documented in README alongside them. Proven to fail, not just to pass: exit 0 on the repaired tree (20 skills), exit 1 on a tampered file, exit 1 on a file added without regenerating. On first run it caught a live violation - main's tip a48d0c0 changed skills/todo-db/SKILL.md without touching the lock, last regenerated two commits earlier in 2a510a9.

.github/workflows/verify-lock.yml runs the checker on pull_request and push to main; rung 2 satisfied (grep -rq verify_lock .github/workflows/ exits 0). README gained a 'Lock invariant' section stating the same-commit rule, the failure modes, the regenerate-and-commit-together remedy, and the distinction from the CLI's verify/status/validate. Promoting it to a REQUIRED status check is a branch-protection setting I cannot change from here - flagged in the PR for Joe. Must-preserve held: lock format untouched (only 6 wrong sha256/size values changed; key order and lockedAt intact), CLI compatibility unaffected, commits authored as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>. All work done in an isolated git worktree, so the live ~/.skill-sync checkout - on an unrelated WIP branch and symlinked into ~/.claude/skills - was never switched or dirtied. Rung 1 runs against that live checkout and stays unsatisfiable until PR #13 merges AND the live checkout is on main.
